levels.L2: Fully bridged: the bridge ships the asset/CLI path and detects it, or stock Blender 5.2 already provides the behaviour.
levels.L1: Partial: an asset or operator reproduces the intent but the path differs from GOO, or one manual step remains.
levels.L0: Unreachable: lives in GOO's C++ renderer or Blender's core/UI; the bridge reports it as unavailable.

items.name: Node-group asset library and Add menu
items.rationale: The bridge ships the GOO node groups as assets and the analyzer already lists every GOO group found in a .blend, so the Add-menu section maps 1:1 onto stock Blender 5.2.
items.external_strategy: Bundle the goo-port node groups and expose them from the bridge; analyze reports which GOO groups are present so the report can confirm adoption.

items.name: View-layer overrides and collection force-enable
source_features: Shift-click collection visibility to force-enable children
items.rationale: Both behaviours are pure Python on native properties (ViewLayer.material_override/world_override and hide_viewport/hide_render), so the bridge can expose them without touching the renderer.
items.external_strategy: Bridge operators write the native view-layer and collection properties; the Shift-click gesture itself stays a Blender shortcut and is not simulated.

items.name: Hex Grid texture
source_features: Hex Grid Texture - Cell UV + integer Cell ID
items.rationale: The goo-port group performs real hexagonal tiling (two offset rectangular lattices, nearest-centre distance field) and was validated visually, so the texture is complete rather than an approximation.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Hex Grid node group; analyze detects it by name and the report marks it green.

items.name: Twirl texture
items.rationale: The group is an exact 2D rotation around the centre with a smooth radial falloff, so it fully reproduces the GOO node.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Twirl node group and let the report verify its presence.

items.name: Grease Pencil auto-close strokes
items.rationale: Setting the CURVE cyclic flag on selected strokes is a complete reproduction of the authoring result; only the while-drawing timing differs.
items.external_strategy: Bridge operator writes the native cyclic flag; the report cannot inspect GP attributes, so the item is marked manual at scan time.

items.name: Viewport line width 1.0-3.0
items.rationale: A draw handler with gpu.state.line_width_set reproduces the viewport result; it is viewport-only by nature, exactly like GOO.
items.external_strategy: Bridge preference plus viewport draw handler; final renders are unaffected, as in GOO.

items.name: Scene camera override control
source_features: Scene camera drop-down in the top bar
items.rationale: The bridge reads and writes native scene.camera and the analyzer records the active camera, so camera switching works even though the widget lives in a bridge panel instead of the top bar.
items.external_strategy: Bridge panel and CLI --camera write scene.camera; analyze records active_camera and the report marks this item green when a camera is set.

items.name: Film transparency toggle
source_features: Transparency toggle in the World tab
items.rationale: Toggling scene.render.film_transparent is the complete native behaviour; only the panel location differs.
items.external_strategy: Bridge checkbox writes film_transparent; the rendered alpha is the native Blender result.

items.name: Topology Mirror toggle
source_features: Topology Mirror next to X/Y/Z mirror
items.rationale: A toggle on the native use_mirror_topology property reproduces the mesh-editing behaviour completely.
items.external_strategy: Bridge operator writes use_mirror_topology; like GOO it only affects armature/mirror editing, not rendering.

items.name: Render burn-in (frame + file name)
items.rationale: The bridge CLI burns Blender's native stamp into PNG output, which matches the GOO result for the supported formats and is fully automated.
items.external_strategy: Bridge render command enables use_stamp, stamp_note/stamp_frame and scales the stamp for PNG output; EXR and light-group composites keep the documented limitation.

items.name: Light Groups workflow and compositing
source_features: Light Groups - name-based groups on lights/materials, per-group shadow toggle, default group
items.rationale: The bridge owns the whole workflow (group data, per-group renders and a linear composite) and the analyzer reports the light-group feature flag, so end-to-end it is complete; only the data path differs from GOO's C++ light loops.
items.external_strategy: Bridge metadata plus multi-pass render and linear composite reproduce the image (mean diff near 1e-6); analyze flags compositor/light-group nodes and the report marks it green.

items.name: Cross-platform pure-Python support
items.rationale: The bridge is standard-library Python plus a Blender subprocess, so it runs wherever Blender 5.2 runs; no platform binaries exist.
items.external_strategy: No action needed: the bridge reports this capability as always present and documents Windows 11 as the verified platform.

items.name: GOO Shader Info and Check Self Shadowing flag
source_features: Shader Info - Diffuse Shading / Cast Shadows / Self Shadows / Ambient Lighting / Half-lambert factor
items.rationale: The shipped group uses Diffuse BSDF -> Shader to RGB with AO proxies for the shadow masks, while GOO evaluates the terms per light in C++; the self-shadowing flag is metadata only, so visual parity is close but not identical.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Shader Info asset with its Check Self Shadowing input; analyze detects the group and the report marks it yellow with the AO-proxy caveat.

items.name: Set Depth shader
source_features: Set Depth - push a shader's pixel depth
items.rationale: The group encodes normalised depth from Camera Data View Z for an EXR/AOV pass; EEVEE cannot write gl_FragDepth from Python, so the pixel-depth push itself is not reproduced.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Set Depth asset and consume its Depth socket via the bridge's depth pass; the report names the missing real depth-buffer write.

items.name: Light Info (legacy and New) drivers
source_features: Light Info (legacy) - chosen light's Color/Power/Perceptual Power
items.rationale: Value sockets plus drivers reading the active light object approximate GOO's compile-time uniforms; they update live, but group interfaces cannot carry an Object reference in Blender 5.2, so the light is chosen by an operator instead of a socket.
items.external_strategy: Ship both Light Info assets and the light-info operators that write energy/color/specular/location/rotation drivers; analyze detects the groups and the report marks them yellow.

items.name: Screen Space Info
source_features: Screen Space Info - Scene Color / Scene Depth
items.rationale: Screen Position, Screen UV, View Depth, View Distance, World Position, Facing, Fresnel and Camera Vector are reconstructed from TexCoord, Camera Data, Geometry and Layer Weight; EEVEE Next does not expose scene colour/depth buffers to shaders.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Screen Space Info asset and pair it with the bridge's depth pass; analyze detects the group and the report marks it yellow.

items.name: Curvature
items.rationale: Narrow-minus-wide Ambient Occlusion plus Layer Weight Fresnel approximates screen-space curvature; ordering (convex > 0.5, flat = 0.5, creases < 0.5) is preserved but the radius response differs from GOO.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Curvature asset; analyze detects it and the report marks it yellow with the AO/Fresnel note.

items.name: SDF shape primitives
items.rationale: The shipped group covers eight representative shapes instead of GOO's 44, so common primitives work while the full shape catalogue does not.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO SDF Primitive asset; analyze detects it by group name and the report marks it yellow with the reduced shape list.

items.name: SDF operations, vector ops and noise
items.rationale: The three groups implement eight operations, eight modifiers and an fBM distance perturbation respectively; the set is representative rather than exhaustive.
items.external_strategy: Ship GOO SDF Op, SDF Vector Op and SDF Noise assets; analyze flags any SDF group and the report marks the cluster yellow.

items.name: Water Ripples
source_features: Water Ripples - Drops / Ripples / Flow / Caustic
items.rationale: The single radial sine field with exponential decay matches the Ripples mode but has no Drops/Flow/Caustic switch, so only one of GOO's four behaviours is approximated.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Water Ripples asset; analyze detects it and the report marks it yellow, naming the missing modes.

items.name: OKLab Color Ramp
items.rationale: The group uses the exact OKLab matrix but only four stops, while GOO exposes an arbitrary-stop ramp widget.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO OKLab Color Ramp asset; analyze flags any OKLab group and the report marks it yellow with the stop-count limit.

items.name: Scene Time (Start/End Frame)
source_features: Scene Time - Start Frame / End Frame
items.rationale: A GeometryNodeTree exposes native Seconds/Frame and refreshes Start/End Frame through frame_change_pre/render_pre handlers; the values are correct but the refresh is a handler side effect rather than a renderer uniform.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Scene Time group plus its handlers; analyze reports the scene_time flag and the report marks it yellow.

items.name: Active Camera geometry-node override
items.rationale: The GOO Active Camera group switches between the override Object and the scene camera with native nodes; native Active Camera nodes created outside the group still read scene.camera because C++ injection is impossible.
items.external_strategy: Ship the GOO Active Camera asset and offer --camera in the bridge CLI; analyze reports active_camera_override and the report marks it yellow.

items.name: Grease Pencil texture randomize and sculpt smoothing
source_features: Texture Mapping randomize - Stroke/Fill offset, scale, rotation, seed
items.rationale: Operators write a per-stroke attribute for material variation and run Laplacian smoothing on the current drawing; GOO instead randomises the texture transform and blends smoothing into the sculpt brush, so the data path differs.
items.external_strategy: Bridge operators provide both tools; the report cannot inspect GP attributes, so the item is marked manual at scan time.

items.name: Pose authoring utilities
items.rationale: Operators hide/restore unselected bones, set the per-axis invert flags and copy constraints by bone name; GOO's isolate mode is modal and its merge walks selected bones across objects, so behaviour is close but not identical.
items.external_strategy: Bridge pose operators cover the three workflows; the report marks them manual because pose state is not part of the analyze JSON.

items.name: Shadow-map internals (shadow ID buffer, contact shadows, bias/CSM/light cache)
source_features: Shadow ID High ID Bit Depth (32-bit shadow IDs)
Shadow buffer bias / Cascaded Shadow Maps / light-cache bake UI
items.rationale: EEVEE Next exposes no shadow-ID buffer, contact-shadow controls, light-cache bake or shadow-bias API; these live in GOO's C++ renderer and cannot be reached from Python.
items.external_strategy: The report marks them red and points at the native-extension C++ route; the bridge can still bake shadows in an external pass if a project needs them.

items.name: Alpha-blended holdout for transparent materials
items.rationale: Blender 5.2 holdout is a whole-object mask; there is no alpha-blend holdout in EEVEE, and the compositor cannot reconstruct it from stock passes.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable; use a cryptomatte/object-index mask in an external composite when needed.

items.name: EEVEE view-layer sample override
items.rationale: ViewLayer.samples follows Cycles semantics and is ignored by EEVEE; EEVEE samples come from scene.eevee.taa_render_samples, so a per-view-layer override cannot be expressed.
items.external_strategy: The bridge exposes scene-level --samples and reports the per-layer override as unavailable.

items.name: Radiance buffer copy between refraction passes
source_features: Radiance buffer copied between Refraction passes
items.rationale: The refraction radiance buffer is a GOO renderer internal with no public 5.2 API.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable; approximate with screen-space refraction compositing externally if required.

items.name: Principled/SSS shader internals
items.rationale: GPU_MATFLAG_PRINCIPLED_* flags and use_sss are internal C++ shader state, not exposed to Blender Python.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable; rely on stock Principled BSDF terms and document the difference.

items.name: Screen-space shadows and refraction internals
items.rationale: These are GOO renderer passes with no equivalent node or Python hook in EEVEE Next.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable; the bridge depth/mist passes only approximate the result.

items.name: Float socket inputs accept inf / -inf
items.rationale: Blender socket defaults reject non-finite floats, a core RNA limitation that no pure-Python add-on can bypass.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable; builders should clamp to large finite values instead of infinity.

items.name: Continuous Trackball navigation
items.rationale: Trackball input and transform behaviour is implemented in Blender's C++ viewport core and cannot be reimplemented from Python.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable; users keep Blender's native navigation.

items.name: Library Override Resync Enforce ignores Action ID pointers
source_features: Library Override Resync Enforce ignores Action ID pointers
items.rationale: Resync Enforce is C++ library-override logic; Python can only observe the resulting overrides.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable and document manual resync handling for linked rigs.

items.name: Outliner hidden-bone row filter
source_features: Hide pose bones / Outliner hidden-bones filter
items.rationale: The per-bone flag is reproduced on an ID property and shown in the bridge pose panel, but Blender 5.2 has no Outliner row-filter hook, so the filter row itself is missing.
items.external_strategy: Store and expose the flag, and mark the row filter as manual/unsupported detail in the report.

items.name: Disable Search on Key Press
items.rationale: Add-menu search behaviour is C++ key handling; there is no Python preference or callback that can suppress it.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable; note the native shortcut workaround in the documentation.

items.name: Grease Pencil 3.0
items.rationale: Grease Pencil v3 is native in Blender 5.2, and all bridge GP tools are written against GP v3 data, so nothing needs porting.
items.external_strategy: Mark as native in the report; no asset or operator is required.

items.name: Material icon rendering and VSE relative-path strips
source_features: Option to turn off material icon rendering
Linked scene strips with relative paths in the VSE
items.rationale: Material thumbnails are drawn in C++ Outliner code, and VSE strip path handling is core C++; neither is reachable from Python.
items.external_strategy: Report as unavailable; keep native icon/path behaviour and document the difference.

items.name: Scene camera drop-down in the top bar
source_features: Scene camera drop-down in the top bar
items.rationale: The camera can be switched from a bridge panel or CLI, but Blender's top bar cannot be extended from Python, so the exact GOO widget placement is impossible.
items.external_strategy: Provide the panel/CLI control and mark the top-bar placement as a documented UI deviation.
